key_reasoning.reason: A new shared feature_gate.py chokepoint (ensure_budget_management_enabled / require_budget_management_enabled) is reused across budget_router.py's router, project_budget_router.py's two routers (router + group_router), and get_cost_center_budget_summary()'s own call — 3-4 components spanning Config, Service, and API layers, with a shared utility deliberately introduced to prevent drift.

The enterprise-ceiling pattern (is_enterprise AND yaml-declared flag) directly reuses the existing Component/CONFIG_IDS mechanism already applied to enterpriseEdition/metricsAnalytics, which argues for a lower score. But the gating is authorization-style access control (403 on missing feature), and a dedicated follow-up commit ('Fix budgetManagement guard bypass for empty-project cost centers') shows the first pass left a real gap the precedent didn't cover — this matches the 'affects authentication or authorization' red flag, bumping from M to L.

diffstat reports 12 files changed (5 src: customer_config.py, budget_router.py, project_budget_router.py, cost_center_budget_summary.py, and the new feature_gate.py; 7 tests: 6 modified + the new test_feature_gate.py). Per the actual-mode N-files-to-score mapping this lands in the 11-15 (XL) band. Flagging a disagreement with the nearest M calibration example (epmcdme-10203, 6 files, total 15): that example's smaller file count kept it mid-M, while this change's heavier test surface (7 of 12 files) pushes the raw count into XL even though the production-code delta is a small, well-patterned shared gate plus four call sites.
